text: In the flashcard design, why does `Deck.review` take the day as a parameter instead of calling the clock?
choices: Date handling belongs in the scheduler, which already receives the current day.
The JVM's clock call is expensive enough to dominate the cost of a review.
A class that reads the clock cannot be tested without waiting, and time is a common source of untestable code.
Reading the clock inside a method makes it impossible to mark the method static.
explanation: It is one of the highest-value habits in the chapter. Passing the day in means every scenario — a card due tomorrow, a card overdue by a week — is one line in a test rather than a wait or a mocked system clock. It is the same move as taking the `Scheduler` in the constructor: push the decision outward so that the class depends on data rather than on the environment.
